AlternateTargets: the dog has no buddha-nature saying
Senses.Note: No direct definition formula of the forms 'X is,' 'what is called X,' or 'what is X' was found, except one later question, 'What is “a dog has no buddha-nature”?' (如何是狗子無佛性), answered 'fishing' (釣). The term's stable corpus function is instead visible in headings, raised-case labels, verses, questions, and later reports about Zhaozhou's recorded case. The full earlier exchange and the later compound title are related evidence, not two meanings.

Occurrences.Kwic: 趙州狗子無佛性。頌云。有問狗佛性。趙州答曰無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (大慧普覺禪師語錄): the headword is an impersonal editorial case-and-verse heading; Dahui Zonggao authors the following verse, while Zhaozhou Congshen is the historical case figure and quoted answerer.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 趙州狗子無佛性 followed by 頌云 is a heading introducing a verse, not direct speech; only the embedded answer 無 is assigned to Zhaozhou.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。舉狗子無佛性話。乃曰。二八佳人刺繡遲。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈會元): Zhongtianzhu Zhongren is the exact speaker in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 以狗子無佛性話。舉無字而提撕。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (五燈會元): Jianfu Wuben is the exact speaker in the complete case.

Occurrences.Kwic: 慧舉狗子無佛性話問之。公擬答。慧以竹篦便打。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (續傳燈錄): the lamp-record compiler narrates that Dahui Zonggao raised the case to Wu Weiming; Dahui is the person described and raiser, not the utterer of the recorder's sentence.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 慧舉…問之 is third-person narration: Dahui is the grammatical subject of the reported raising, while the compiler owns the headword-bearing sentence.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：如何是狗子無佛性？王云：釣。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (御選語錄): an unnamed participant asks 'What is the dog-has-no-buddha-nature case?'; the Yongzheng Emperor supplies the reply.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: 問 introduces the unnamed participant's headword-bearing question; 王云 introduces the Yongzheng Emperor's one-word reply 釣.

Occurrences.Kwic: 五祖道趙州狗子無佛性。也勝猫兒十萬倍。如何。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao is the exact speaker of this headword-bearing statement.

Occurrences.Kwic: 當晚來室中只問渠箇狗子無佛性話。便去不得
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao is the exact speaker of this headword-bearing statement.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 僧問：「狗子有佛性也無？」師云：「你有佛性也無？」
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source text (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄): Juelang Daosheng is the exact speaker of this anchored contrast.

Senses.Explanation: The expression is a case-title and saying built from Zhaozhou's recorded answer 'no' when asked whether a dog has buddha-nature. The phrase serves as a title or shorthand for the recorded exchange in which someone asks whether a dog has buddha-nature and Zhaozhou answers 'no.' Dahui's verse heading states 'Zhaozhou: a dog has no buddha-nature' (趙州狗子無佛性) and immediately restates the exchange as 'someone asked about a dog's buddha-nature; Zhaozhou answered, no' (有問狗佛性。趙州答曰無). Other records raise 'the saying that a dog has no buddha-nature' (狗子無佛性話), quote its word 'no' (無字), use it in questioning, and place it beside the separately attested wording 'a dog has buddha-nature' (狗子有佛性). The word 'no' is translated as English 'no.'
